meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Continental European codified system; company law governed by the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (freedom of establishment, provision of services, and free movement of capital)

Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) bilateral investment treaty network covering approximately 60 jurisdictions, including Hong Kong SAR, Russia, India, Egypt, Mexico, and various African and Middle Eastern states

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: AML/CFT regime is governed by the Luxembourg Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as consolidated and amended, notably by the Law of 17 July 2020 transposing Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843, together with implementing Grand-Ducal regulations and CSSF circulars applicable to supervised professionals. The beneficial ownership register (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs, 'REBE') was established by the Law of 13 January 2019 and amended by the Law of 2 June 2024 in response to ECJ judgments C-37/20 and C-601/20, which invalidated general public access. Company law for the SARL is governed by the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended (Article 710-1 et seq.), requiring notarial incorporation, a minimum share capital of EUR 12,350, and at least 25% payment of subscribed parts. Registration formalities are governed by the Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS) and the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA). The statutory UBO disclosure trigger is direct or indirect ownership of more than 25% of capital or voting rights (in practice interpreted as 25% plus one share or one voting right), or control through other means as defined by Article 1 of the Law of 13 January 2019.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (post-2024 REBE regime: full and direct access is reserved to Luxembourg authorities, the Financial Intelligence Unit (CRF), notaries, lawyers, and regulated AML-obliged entities acting within customer due diligence processes; general public searchability has been removed, with access possible only upon demonstrated legitimate interest; in substance the register is not publicly searchable)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies register or trade registry in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961 Convention; Luxembourg acceded in 1979); for non-Convention origin states, full consular legalization chain through the competent consulate and the Luxembourg Ministry of Foreign Affairs

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the corporate resolution of each foreign corporate shareholder authorizing the incorporation of the Luxembourg SARL, and notarized power of attorney appointing the person to appear before the Luxembourg notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or equivalent governing body of the corporate shareholder in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in the country of origin followed by Hague Apostille; for non-Convention states, consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copies of valid passports and proof of residential address of all ultimate beneficial owners, proposed managers (gérants), and authorized signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin, or the issuing competent authority in the case of certified identity documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified notarial copies legalized by Hague Apostille or consular legalization where the executing notary is outside Luxembourg

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Blocked-account bank attestation certifying the deposit of the minimum share capital of EUR 12,350, opened by the incorporator or its attorney in fact at a Luxembourg or EEA credit institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed credit institution holding the blocked contribution account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original signed banker's letter delivered directly to the Luxembourg notary; no apostille required, but the bank must apply standard AML/KYC verification

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Source-of-funds statement and AML/KYC questionnaire covering the full funding chain of each subscriber to the share capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Preparing counsel, the Luxembourg notary, and the subscribing shareholder acting jointly
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original statement executed by the shareholder; if executed abroad, notarized and apostilled in accordance with the Hague Convention

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory multi-list screening of every UBO, manager (gérant), authorized signatory, and intermediate corporate holder against the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (CFSP), the OFAC SDN List (reflecting USD wire-rail and Stripe payment routing exposure), and domestic integrity notices published by the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (CRF). PEP identification follows Article 3(9) of Directive (EU) 2015/849, as amended, and FATF Recommendation 12; identified PEPs trigger enhanced due diligence, written source-of-wealth documentation, and senior-management approval. Designated persons, entities subject to asset freezes, sanctioned jurisdictions, and artificial ownership chains lacking economic substance are disqualifying factors for incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), online at www.lbrc.lu, including the national e-Justice name-blocking module and the Guichet.lu single-window portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The RCS operates in French; notarial deeds and statutory filings are drafted in French. Corporate names must be expressed in Latin script; French, German, Luxembourgish, and English elements are accepted, while non-Latin scripts require complete romanization. Accented characters are permitted. The legal-form suffix 'Société à responsabilité limitée' or the abbreviation 'SARL' must appear in the registered name and must be unambiguous. The name must not mislead as to the corporate object or public status, and must be clearly distinguishable from existing RCS-registered names and protected trademarks.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque, Bank, Banking, Dépôt — reserved for CSSF-authorized credit institutions and requiring prior regulatory clearance
Assurance, Réassurance, Insurance — reserved for undertakings authorized by the Commissariat aux Assurances (CAA)
OPCVM, SICAV, SICAF, FCP, Fonds de placement, Fonds d'investissement — reserved for Luxembourg investment-fund vehicles requiring CSSF pre-approval
État, étatique, Grand-Ducal, Gouvernement, municipal, commune — tokens evoking the State, the Grand-Ducal House, or public authorities, requiring prior ministerial or communal consent
Bourse, chambre de compensation, clearing, exchange, settlement — regulated-market markers requiring CSSF or Ministry of Finance assessment

Finance, Syndicate, Securities, Trading — not prohibited per se, but treated as sensitive descriptors triggering an ordre-public and consumer-deception review; acceptable only where the declared corporate object (ISIC 6391 financial news aggregation and syndication feed) explicitly disclaims licensable financial-market activity
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On RCS refusal, the applicant shall (i) obtain written grounds of refusal from the RCS registrar; (ii) file a curative resubmission within 15 days, attaching disclaimer letters, consent declarations from prior name holders, or disambiguating affixes; and (iii) if the registrar maintains the refusal, appeal to the Tribunal d'Arrondissement de Luxembourg (commercial chamber) under the Law of 19 December 2002 and the applicable Code de commerce procedures, or alternatively initiate summary proceedings (référé) before the President of the court. The applicant may simultaneously file a de novo application with a materially distinctive secondary name while preserving its appeal rights.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted only through a licensed professional domiciliation agent operating under the Law of 31 May 1999 on domiciliation activities. For an ISIC 6391 financial news aggregation and syndication feed company classified as Low_Risk_Standard, a virtual office at the licensed agent's address satisfies RCS registration at inception, but does not by itself establish corporate-tax residence or commercial substance. The SARL must maintain locally accessible books and records, a locally resident manager or equivalent operational presence, and actual equipment or contractual infrastructure supporting the newswire API service; otherwise the RCS and Luxembourg tax authorities may recharacterize the registered office and the company may face substance-related audit risk.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low. Quantified risk is approximately 4-8% annual probability of an unannounced RCS or CRF verification visit, with a cumulative likelihood of 10-15% over the first 36 months for a non-licensed, low-risk news-wire SARL domiciled with a licensed agent. Inspection probability increases where UBO chains involve multiple non-EEA intermediate layers, where the declared registered office is purely virtual, or where REBE filings are incomplete or inconsistent.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 100 et seq. concerning the Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), operating under the Ministry of Justice; public announcements are published in the Electronic Compendium of Companies and Associations (RESA)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) containing the articles of association (statuts) and the subscription statements
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum subscribed share capital is EUR 12,000. Cash contributions must be paid up to at least 25% of each share before filing, with the paid amount deposited into a blocked bank account in the company's name; in-kind contributions must be fully paid up and are subject to statutory auditor review when required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: After due convening and quorum, the sole director/shareholder committee of the Société à Responsabilité Limitée in formation resolves: (1) The subscription list annexed to the notarial deed is approved in full; each subscriber subscribes to the shares set opposite their name and pays the required fraction of capital into the designated blocking account. (2) The registered office is adopted at 12, Rue de la Bourse, L-2416 Luxembourg. (3) Mr. Jean-Pierre Dupont is appointed sole Manager with sole signature authority; Mrs. Anna Kowalski is appointed alternate manager and AML contact. (4) Both are authorized to execute all filings with the RCS and Guichet unique.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the incorporation deed and adoption of articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Civil-law notary in Luxembourg City, acting under the Chamber of Notaries; final statutory registration follows with the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalize the draft articles of association and capital subscription schedule with counsel. Schedule a notarial appointment before a Luxembourg notary. Execute the notarial incorporation deed containing the statutes, the subscription list, the registered office address, and the appointment of the first Manager. The notary verifies the identity and civil capacity of all subscribers and checks the legal object of the company.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association (Statuts) in French, German or English
Capital subscription schedule listing each subscriber and number of shares
Passport or national identity document of each subscriber and manager
Consent letter or lease title for the proposed registered office
Draft first board resolution or shareholder minutes
Anti-money-laundering declarations required by the notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises a query on the legal object or on capital subscription terms, amend the draft statutes and resubmit; if the deed is rejected, a corrected deed can be re-executed without disclosing the query to the RCS.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of blocked capital account and deposit of paid-up capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg licensed credit institution or bank selected by the founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a company-in-formation account in the name of 'SARL in formation' and simultaneously block the account exclusively for the benefit of the future company. Deposit the required fraction of cash capital. Obtain from the bank an attestation of blockage (attestation de blocage) addressed to the notary, stating the amount credited and the blocking instructions.
required_dossiers: Draft notarial deed or preliminary incorporation file
Identification documents of account signatories
Beneficial ownership declaration under the Luxembourg Law of 13 January 2019
Bank KYC forms and source-of-funds evidence
Proof of address of the company in formation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional source-of-funds information, provide supplementary bank statements or documented asset history. If unwilling, select another licensed bank and re-open the account; the 25% paid-up fraction may be funded from any lawful source.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the RCS and publication in RESA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), accessible through the e-RCS/e-filing portal; publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarization, electronically file with the RCS the notarial deed, the attestation de blocage and the registration form Fiche électronique (Form A). Pay the registration fee. Upon successful review, the RCS issues the Luxembourg business registration number. The notary or filing agent then triggers publication of the incorporation extract in RESA, which produces legal effect against third parties.
required_dossiers: Notarized incorporation deed
Bank attestation of blocked capital
Fiche électronique / Form A signed by the Manager
Identification and addresses of the Manager and alternate manager
Extract from the criminal record or equivalent of managers when requested
Proof of payment of the state filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS raises a query, cure the deficiency through the e-RCS file within 15 days. If the registration is refused or lapses, submit a new filing together with a statement that no change has occurred since the notarial deed; publication in RESA may be re-secured through the same file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business establishment permit application for commercial activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy – Direction générale des PME, via the Guichet unique (Single Permit Point) at guichet.public.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the online 'autorisation d'établissement' application for the activity of news agency, data processing and financial information syndication. Attach the RCS registration certificate, identity and criminal record of the Manager, and a signed honesty declaration. The qualification requirement for non-craft commercial activities is deemed met by general education; an administrative fee is charged. Await the ministerial decision.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate (extrait du registre de commerce)
Criminal record of each managing person or commitment to provide it
Identity card or passport of the Manager
Curriculum vitae for competence assessment when requested
Registered office lease or ownership title
Guichet unique electronic application form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the permit application is queried, respond through the Guichet unique portal with additional explanations. If refused, file an administrative reconsideration with the Minister of the Economy within one month of notification or bring an action before the administrative tribunal; the decision remains suspended during review only if expressly granted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Ancillary registrations with the social security, VAT and statistical authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); STATEC via MyGuichet
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Enroll the company as an employer with the CCSS if the first employee is hired or immediately upon starting payroll. Register for VAT with the AEDT using the VAT form for new businesses, indicating the supply of financial newswire services which may be subject to reverse charge or e-services VAT rules. Submit the annual statistics declaration to STATEC if required based on employees or turnover.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate
Manager's identification
Bank account details
VAT registration form or electronic counterpart
Employment contracts register summary if any hire exists
EORI number application if the company undertakes cross-border movements
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CCSS registration is delayed, submit the employer declaration retroactively with justification and pay any late surcharge. For AEDT VAT allocation, any delay may result in an estimate of taxable turnover; file a correction declaration to align the VAT effective date.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – Direction générale des PME and the Guichet unique for commercial establishment permits; industrial and workplace inspection falls under the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) and the Ministry of the Interior for physical site compliance
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Business Establishment Permit) under the amended Law of 2 September 2011 on access to trades and crafts

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency), under the Ministry of Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – the financial newswire and data aggregation service is an office-based activity not listed in the annexes of the Law of 15 May 2008 on environmental impact assessment; no EIA screening or EIA report is required unless an in-house data center installation exceeds thresholds for electrical or cooling equipment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source industrial discharges; general municipal sewage standards apply for office washrooms. If a small server or cooling plant is installed, thermal and cooling system permits are required under the Code of Environment, and any volatile organic compound or refrigerant leak must be reported under Regulation (EU) No 517/2014; waste electrical and electronic equipment must be returned to approved collection channels under the WEEE law.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: A fire-safety certificate for the registered office is required from the local commune fire inspection and the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) before occupation if the premises are used for continuous data operations; structural load clearance is required for any false-floor or server room, and an occupational health registration with a certified external prevention service and ITM work-closure approval are needed when hiring employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direct taxation: Administration des contributions directes (ACD), Luxembourg Direct Tax Authority (45 boulevard Roosevelt, L-2983 Luxembourg); indirect taxation and VAT registration: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); customs supervision: Administration des douanes et accises. Official electronic portal: guichet.lu / myGuichet; business registration platform: Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (lbr.lu); VAT filings and authorisations: AEDT e-TVA platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Execute the notarized deed of incorporation of the SARL and deposit it with the Luxembourg Business Registers for inscription in the Trade and Companies Register (RCSL). 2) Upon inscription, the ACD automatically attributes the RNE national identification number (matricule), which simultaneously serves as the corporate income tax, net wealth tax and employer withholding tax account number; no separate income-tax registration is required for the SARL. 3) For VAT, file the dematerialized VAT registration application with the AEDT through the e-TVA/myGuichet channel; a manager, legal representative or duly mandated tax adviser may file; the AEDT delivers the LU-prefixed 8-digit VAT number, normally within 5 to 15 working days, and simultaneously enrols the taxpayer in the periodical VAT return circuit. 4) A foreign non-established entrepreneur whose supplies are taxable in Luxembourg must register before the first taxable supply, unless the transaction falls within the EU OSS, non-EU OSS or Import One-Stop-Shop (IOSS); the AEDT may request the appointment of a Luxembourg-based tax representative where the applicant has no EU establishment and no EU residence. 5) Non-resident shareholders of the SARL are not subject to registration; the SARL is the taxpayer and, where applicable, withholds at source on distributions paid. 6) After registration, the SARL must display the matricule and VAT number on all invoices, customs declarations and OSS returns and maintain an electronic archive of registration certificates.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg applies no US-style check-the-box election; the SARL is legally opaque and automatically subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités), municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal) and net wealth tax (impôt sur la fortune) on its worldwide income, unless the residence tie-breaker in an applicable double tax treaty relocates fiscal residence. Elective regimes available to the SARL include: (a) VAT grouping (assujetti unique) on application to the AEDT, limited to Luxembourg-established taxable persons; (b) waiver of VAT exemption on real-estate lettings and transfers under the VAT Law; (c) IP Box relief under Article 50bis of the Income Tax Law (LIR), granting an 80% exemption on qualifying net IP income with OECD Nexus-compliant tracking; (d) EU OSS, non-EU OSS and IOSS elections for distance sales and business-to-consumer electronically supplied services; (e) substantive, non-elective participation exemption on dividends and capital gains where the qualifying holding and holding-period conditions are met; (f) hybrid-mismatch treatment is mandatory and non-elective under the ATAD 2 transposition of 21 December 2017, with no check-the-box override available.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating within the Eurosystem and pursuant to Article 107 TFEU, Council Regulation (EC) No 1103/97 and Regulation (EC) No 974/98; banking supervision is delegated to the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF), while the BCL maintains the balance-of-payments statistical reporting obligation for cross-border flows above EUR 12,500 per individual transaction under the BCL 'Reporting on External Statistics' framework (BOINB/LU reporting circulars).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro (EUR) enjoys unrestricted convertibility in Luxembourg. As a Eurozone member state implementing Articles 63-66 TFEU on free movement of capital and Article VIII of the IMF Articles of Agreement, Luxembourg applies zero exchange-control restrictions on either current account (subscription revenues, trade settlements, operating expenses) or capital account (equity injections, shareholder loans, dividend repatriation, liquidation proceeds) transactions. No prior CSSF, BCL, or Ministry of Finance authorisation is required for inbound or outbound transfers denominated in EUR or foreign currency. Practical profit remittance hurdles are limited to taxation, not conversion: a Luxembourg SARL distributing dividends triggers 15% domestic withholding tax, which is reduced to 0% when the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (Directive 2011/96/EU) applies, or mitigated under bilateral double-tax treaties (e.g., 5% rate under the 1996 Luxembourg-USA treaty on portfolio dividends of 10% or more shareholding). Corporate treasury operations may repatriate capital and advance intercompany loans freely; the BCL only requests statistical declaration via the e-file portal COREP/liquidity declarations for transactions exceeding EUR 12,500, not as a permission-based control. Sanctions screening (CSSF-issued EU/UN restrictive measures list) and CBUAE-style reporting are the only quotidian compliance duties, neither operating as a quantifiable limitation on convertibility.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable — no statutory timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio exist in Luxembourg. The Corporation of the Belgian-Luxembourg Economic Union, and Luxembourg in particular, abandoned export-proceeds surrender obligations upon accession to the OECD Code of Liberalisation of Capital Movements. For the target SARL's cross-border newswire subscription revenue (the economic equivalent of 'export proceeds' for a services/API sale), the EUR-denominated incoming SWIFT MT103s or SEPA SCT Inst payments may be retained freely in EUR, converted at any time via any authorized FX counterparty, or transferred to any third-party payee without any BCL haircut or conversion quota. The only legal filing is statistical: a monthly balance-of-payments declaration via BCL 'Reporting on External Statistics' web interface when aggregate receipts/payments with non-residents exceed EUR 12,500, submitted within 30 days, with no obligation to convert, retain, or surrender a defined percentage to the monetary authority.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Custody and Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High as a collection rail, Medium as a treasury settlement hub; the SARL must maintain its primary domiciliation account at a fully licensed Luxembourg credit institution (CSSF authorised as a credit institution under the Law of 5 April 1993). Offshore digital EMIs (Paysafe, Airwallex, Payoneer, Revolut Business, Stripe) can lawfully provide payment collection under the PSD2 payment institution/EMI licence passed into Luxembourg by the CSSF, but none may accept deposits (deposit-taking is statutorily reserved to credit institutions per Article 1 of the Law of 5 April 1993). Legal constraints: (i) an EMI must ring-fence client funds in a safeguard account at a regulated credit institution, making the SARL's treasury dependent on an underlying bank account anyway; (ii) payment institutions are excluded from interbank settlement membership at BCL TARGET2 and cannot furnish MT103 corporate-clearing guarantees; (iii) input VAT/receivable financing via bank discount is inoperable with EMI accounts; therefore the blueprint mandates a Tier-1 bank account as the primary treasury controller with Stripe as a permitted card/API-based collection conduit wired onward via the PSP's settlement account at a partner bank (e.g., Stripe's Deutsche Bank Luxembourg or JP Morgan settlement line).
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a newly incorporated Luxembourg SARL with non-resident UBOs, a fully remote account opening is generally not accepted by CSSF-supervised banks. Standard mandate: at least one natural-person director or a duly appointed local authorised signatory (resident in Luxembourg or an EU/EEA state) must attend a face-to-face meeting at the bank's Luxembourg branch or with a bank relationship manager in the country, either before account activation or within 10 business days thereafter as a 'conditional remote KYC with mandatory verification visit'. The absence of any physical presence can be partially remedied by: (a) executing a notarised power of attorney (procuration) before a Luxembourg notary; (b) presenting a notarised board resolution of the SARL approving the account opening with specimen signatures certified through apostille (not sufficient alone); and (c) commissioning an independent AML/KYC agent report (e.g., a Luxembourg law firm or an approved ACD/AMLD actor) to perform video identification in compliance with the Luxembourg AML Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Regulation 12-02. Mitigation for the newswire business: because ISIC 6391 is a non-financial low-risk activity, the onboarding committee generally accepts a pragmatic hybrid — one remote interview with the director plus one in-person attendance by a local fiduciary agent holding a valid passport and a power of attorney — while still reserving the right to summon the director for a final compliance interview in Luxembourg if the beneficial ownership chain exceeds two layers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO identification failing CSSF transparency benchmark — non-resident parent reflected in pre-BEPS-era private foundation with undisclosed settlor; banking AML case officer flags incomplete economic ownership chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bundle: (i) authorised extract from the Luxembourg Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) naming directors and officer's signature; (ii) full UBO declaration in the CSSF/Observatoire RBE format; (iii) a certified corporate-organisation chart sworn before a Luxembourg notary covering each layer to ultimate individual; (iv) passport + proof of residence for each natural-person UBO and director; (v) a notarised statutory declaration of the managing director confirming no PEP status or a documented PEP regime; (vi) 3 years of professional references from a regulated bank, law firm, or Big-4 auditor for the sponsoring group.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds opacity in the initial capital injection — EUR 12,500 minimum share capital paid to the SARL's escrow/blocked account from a third-country parent's account, triggering possible reverse-EDD (politically exposed persons/sanctions exposure on originator bank).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bundle: (i) notarised deed of incorporation and fully subscribed 'part sociale' block; (ii) certified copy of the shareholder's bank-account statement showing the exact inbound credit string and contra-debit; (iii) transfer-purpose filenote (code CAP09 'Capital contribution to non-financial corporation') quoted on the SWIFT MT103; (iv) written confirmation from the parent's home regulator that the remitting bank is duly licensed; (v) if capital is advanced as shareholder loan instead of equity, add a signed loan agreement with arm's-length interest and contemporaneous transfer pricing file per OECD TP Guidelines; (vi) a police/criminal-record certificate for each UBO confirmed by apostille.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Revenue model flagged as 'aggregation of syndicated loan information' capable of being misread as unlicensed financial advice or an unregulated credit platform creating a payment-transparency discrepancy between SWIFT receipts and the corporate description.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bundle: (i) official CSSF no-licence eligibility confirmation obtained by written enquiry — statutory licence requirement under the Law of 5 April 1993 Art. 28-1 excluding news-compilation services; (ii) an ISIC 6391 / NAICS 519110 descriptive memorandum signed by the compliance officer demonstrating non-advice/non-arrangement character; (iii) executed software licence and subscription agreements with customers and data suppliers proving the API-feed commercial model; (iv) a dedicated revenue-reconciliation ledger mapping each SWIFT credit to a specific subscriber invoice; (v) confirmation that the platform does not handle third-party money (no safeguarding obligations under PSD2), evidenced by a written legal opinion attaching the bank-flow chart.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient tangible substance in Luxembourg — bank suspicious of a brass-plate SARL because the registered office uses a service provider address and the entity has zero employees at account-opening date.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bundle: (i) 12-month lease agreement for physical premises in Luxembourg City or a real administrative office with a dedicated receptionist; (ii) SARL board minutes (in French/German/English) showing that treasury decisions are effectively taken in Luxembourg; (iii) payroll intent — an employment contract for an operational manager and proof of social-security enrolment with the Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale; (iv) a Luxembourg VAT registration certificate (TVA no.) and an annual budget; (v) a relationship-bank introduction letter from the accounting firm holding the entity's audit mandate; (vi) CSSF substance questionnaire evidencing that server contracts, subscriber-intake procedures, and cash-flow projections are managed from Luxembourg only.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing: (1) Pre-funding stage — execute the notarised deed of incorporation/share capital increase before a Luxembourg notary; register in RCS; obtain RCS number. (2) Wire stage — the shareholder remits EUR 12,500 (SARL minimum) or any greater agreed capital via SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA SCT Inst for EEA-origin) to the SARL's blocked capital account (compte de non-valeur) at the selected Luxembourg bank. The SWIFT field 70 (Remittance Information) must quote purpose code CAP09 ('equity capital contribution') or LICO2 for intercompany loans, plus the phrase 'DEED OF INCORPORATION OF [insert date] — REGISTERED RCS N°. L[insert]'. Field 50K must name the exact legal shareholder entity; any mismatch between the contributor and the RCS-shareholder list triggers on-hold. (3) Verification stage — deliver to the bank: certified copy of the notarised deed, clearing-court registration certificate, UBO declaration, and the shareholder's payment-order confirmation; the bank credits the permanent operating account after releasing the block and returns a certificate of receipt for accounting/tax file. (4) BCL reporting — the EUR 12,500+ injection must be reported to BCL via the external-statistics declaration within 30 days. For the syndicated-finance-newswire entity, any higher strategic capital (e.g., EUR 500,000 to meet vendor credit references of Tier-1 bank lines) is routed identically, with the bank applying FATCA/CRS attribution to the beneficial owners and performing politically exposed persons screening on the benefit of the funds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails for the ISIC 6391 newswire are professional-service disbursements, not lending operations: (a) SWIFT MT103 for cross-border content-licence royalties, technology-as-a-service fees, marketing payments and legal/audit retainer invoices — quoting purpose codes such as LICO or RATE (services), with the beneficiary bank's BIC and the SARL's own internal reference; (b) SEPA SCT Inst (instant credit transfer) for payments within SEPA; (c) Commercial Letters of Credit — although the SARL is a finance newswire, if a future syndicated-finance asset offset is needed, the SARL may open a standby commercial LC in favour of a data-verification counterpart using a confirmed 'Luxembourg Utilization' documentary credit issued by BIL or BCEE, provided the underlying is a genuine sale-of-goods/news-licence contract; (d) MT202 COV for interbank/bank-to-bank reimbursements arising from treasury sweeps or sub-account concentration, strictly accompanied by MT103 cover; (e) for dividend repatriation to the parent, the SARL uses MT103 with field 72 'withholding tax domestic 15%' or 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive and attaches an E2 tax-form liquidation certificate; and (f) the SARL's outsourced collection rail, Stripe, remits net settlement cash by ACH/SEPA to the Luxembourg corporate account, with daily reconciliation against subscription log files, preserving an audit trail suitable for a syndicated-finance counterparty to verify that no commingling of third-party funds occurs.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla FX Forward (delivery-based, EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF, EUR/JPY) — bilaterally executed under a Luxembourg-law ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or a credit institution's standard FX Terms of Business, generally on a collateralised CSA basis.
FX Swap (double-leg spot-against-forward) — permitted for liquidity management between EUR and USD accounts under a standard FX Swap confirmation and cash-pooling arrangement.

Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swap (CCIRS) — admissible in respect of any future syndicated-finance asset or intercompany borrowing, subject to CSSF CRR leverage/capital treatment and ISDA master authorisation by the board.
Currency Options (European-style) — permissible for treasury budget-rate certainty with a CSSF-authorized FX counterparty; premium payment via MT103 with purpose code FOREX.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) — permitted in principle where the counterparty currency is non-convertible (e.g., SARL affiliate exposed to a soft-currency cashflow), but irrelevant for EUR crosses which clear on a deliverable FX market; any NDF is booked only as a hedge of a specific non-EUR exposure with the settlement in EUR under an existing ISDA/CSSF-governed framework.

metadata_closure.regulatory_mapping_note: Luxembourg is a unitary national jurisdiction with no sub-sovereign tax or banking distinctions; all corporate accounts, FX operations and clearing rails are subject to the single CSSF AML/CFT legal framework (Law of 12 November 2004 as amended by the Law of 25 March 2020) and to EU PSD2, CRD V, CRR, and GDPR considerations applicable to the financial newswire model. The treasury blueprint above is fully interoperable with SWIFT Wire and Stripe as the target rails.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts and, if applicable, auditor's report (LUX GAAP)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) via eJustice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' meeting must approve annual accounts within 6 months of financial year-end; RCS filing must occur within 1 month of approval. For a 31 December financial year-end, AGM by 30 June and RCS filing by 30 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is punishable by commercial court fines typically between EUR 500 and EUR 5,000 per responsible officer; RCS formal reminders and Public Prosecutor referral; persistent default may trigger court-ordered dissolution and administrative striking-off of the RCS file.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a tax year ending 31 December, the corporate income tax return must be filed no later than 31 December of the following calendar year. Extensions may be granted on reasoned request.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Imposition d'office if no return is filed; late-filing surcharge up to 10% of assessed tax; late-payment interest at 0.8% per commenced month; enforced collection by garnishment and legal mortgage; wilful non-compliance may be referred to the Public Prosecutor for criminal tax penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual municipal business tax return (impôt commercial communal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing deadline aligned with the corporate income tax return: for a 31 December year-end, due by 31 December of the following calendar year unless an extension is granted.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Official assessment by ACD if the return is missing; 0.8% monthly late-payment interest; administrative fines and enforced recovery of municipal business tax through attachment of bank accounts and distraint on assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual net wealth tax return (impôt sur la fortune)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 December year-end, the net wealth tax return is due by 31 December of the following calendar year together with the corporate income tax return.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: ACD may impose official assessment and late-filing penalties; interest accrues at 0.8% per commenced month; persistent failure exposes the SARL to enforced collection and criminal fines for deliberate tax non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership register (RBE) update and annual validation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE), administered by the Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month of any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership, the SARL must update the RBE. There is no fixed annual RBE filing date, but the company must perform an annual internal register audit and confirm the RBE data when required by the RBE administration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance with RBE disclosure obligations is punishable by criminal fines up to EUR 125,000 and imprisonment of responsible individuals under the Luxembourg RBE Law; administrative enforcement may also include court action by the Public Prosecutor.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Luxembourg SARL is subject to mandatory independent audit by a réviseur d'entreprises agréé when it exceeds, for two consecutive financial years, at least two of the following thresholds: balance-sheet total EUR 4,400,000; net turnover EUR 8,800,000; average workforce 50 employees. Audit may also be required in cases of public-interest status, group consolidation requirements, or upon shareholder request representing at least 10% of capital.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 on annual accounts is the statutory accounting framework; IFRS as adopted in the EU applies for consolidated accounts where applicable. Annual accounts must be presented in euros.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Luxembourg RBE regime, the SARL must file any share transfer or beneficial ownership change within one month. The company is also required to keep RBE data accurate and, if the RBE administration issues an annual confirmation or data-review notice, to confirm or correct the information within one month. The registered agent should annually reconcile the share register, shareholders' resolutions, and RBE filing as part of the statutory register audit.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (17% CIT + 1.19% solidarity surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax for Luxembourg City)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holidays. Available incentives limited to IP Box regime (80% exemption on net qualifying IP income), participation exemption (100% dividend and capital gains exemption), and special investment credit regimes. Not applicable to financial newswire operations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return Form 1010 (Déclaration de l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) filed electronically via eCIT portal through MyGuichet.lu
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 5 months after the fiscal year-end; for calendar-year entities, due 31 May of the following year. Extension possible until 31 December upon request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year start and end dates (YYYY-MM-DD)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31 or actual truncated fiscal period for first return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business reference number (N° d'identification, RCSC) and RCSL company registration number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide Luxembourg RCSL registration number as shown on the articles of incorporation. For a non-resident-owned SARL, no local agent code required beyond the appointed statutory auditor.
Report accounting profit prepared under Luxembourg GAAP, which may be adjusted via extra-accounting declarations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declared taxable income after legal deductions and participation exemption
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For 100% participation exemption, attach Schedule E and provide permanent establishment or shareholding documentation. Non-resident shareholders do not file individually at entity level.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate tax credits and withholding tax relief claimed
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim foreign tax credits by filing supporting TRC and proof of underlying tax with the return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties: automatic 10% surcharge on assessed tax; an additional €1,000–€5,000 administrative fine for failure to file; interest on late payment at 0.8% per month compounded. Imprisonment possible for fraudulent non-filing.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% (or 5% for parent-resident under Swiss DTA; 0% EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where a 10% qualifying holding is held for at least 12 months)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply reduced DTA rate, the non-resident shareholder must provide to the Luxembourg paying entity before the dividend payment: (i) a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the treaty jurisdiction, (ii) a beneficial ownership declaration (Form 105, 106 or equivalent), and (iii) for reduced EU rate, evidence of shareholding percentage and minimum holding period. The paying company files the withholding tax return and must retain all documentation for 5 years; failure to submit timely documentation leaves the 15% statutory rate applicable with no subsequent reclaim.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% statutory withholding tax on outgoing royalties (no treaty deduction required); Interest: 0% withholding tax on interest, subject to unlike practices for profit-sharing loans which are treated as dividends. For debt interest and royalty payments to EU residents, the Interest-Royalty Directive eliminates tax when 25% ownership is met.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File required if related-party transactions exceed EUR 150,000 for financial (with interest or royalties) or service transactions, and EUR 1 million for other transactions; Master File required when group consolidated revenue exceeds EUR 100 million; CbC report due for groups with EUR 750 million consolidated revenue.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: LU Economic Substance Requirements apply under Luxembourg law according to EU ATAD, OECD BEPS, and administrative guidelines. The SARL must demonstrate adequate personnel, office premises, decision-making in Luxembourg, and accounting records. For a financial newswire operating via API, substantive activities such as contract drafting, data sourcing, invoicing, and server infrastructure must be managed in Luxembourg. Zero-substance shell arrangements face challenge under the 2018 Luxembourg 'Law on the Taxation of Parent and Subsidiary', leading to denial of benefits under DTA, tax residency issues, or penalty of €10,000–€50,000 for missing substance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful understatement of taxable revenue by omitting newsfeed subscription fees or cross-border license payments, or using falsified invoices to shift profit to zero-tax offshore entities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of evaded tax, plus interest (0.8%/month) and penalties: up to 100% of tax deficiency (fraud penalty) and criminal fines up to €250,000. For criminal tax fraud, imprisonment up to 2 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly and severally liable for company tax debts if they were aware of tax evasion; travel bans and asset freezes possible; criminal conviction leads to imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a letterbox company with no physical presence, no employees, no independent management, and no active business decision-making; nominally holding data licences and routing profits outward.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disallowance of tax treaty benefits, denial of Luxembourg tax residence status, exposure to domestic anti-abuse provisions, and administrative fines equal to 5% of the unduly claimed tax advantages. Annual return void, plus forced liquidation proceedings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors held personally liable for the company's unpaid taxes if the shell substance is deemed a sham; a court may order civil restitution of tax advantages and restrict leaving Luxembourg until settlement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting large subscription fees from high-risk non-resident clients without beneficial owner due diligence, or failing to report suspicious transactions in syndicated finance news deals (sanctions risk).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Luxembourg law (AML5/AML6 implementation), administrative penalties up to 5% of global turnover, minimum €10,000, and revocation of the business license. A violation of asset-freeze regulations leads to fine up to €1 million or 10% of total assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors ousted from their position and disqualified from management; criminal liability for money laundering complicity, imprisonment up to 10 years and fine up to €1 million. Liquidators may pierce the veil based on personal fault.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to maintain documentation for intercompany newsfeed data license fees, or making misguided cost-plus calculations with inconsistent markups (e.g., not applying economic analysis to newswire aggregation margins).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary TP adjustment plus secondary adjustment (notional distribution tax at 15%) and penalty of 25% of adjusted profit. Late TP documentation filing triggers €5,000 daily penalty up to a maximum €50,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held jointly liable for tax adjustments if they approved the mispricing; risk of civil restitution actions from foreign tax authorities; in cross-border cases, Interpol red notices for deliberate fraud.
